column3: NASB adds “to worship the LORD,” not in the Hebrew of this verse.
“Let me cause to dwell” is rendered “I will let you dwell”; the Hebrew vowels could also read “let me dwell with you.”
NASB supplies “This is” in the threefold “temple of the LORD.”
NASB adds the question mark; the Hebrew has “so as to do” without a question.
“Here I have seen” is rendered “I, even I, have seen it.”
“For the sake of the shame of their faces” is rendered “to their own shame.”
The Hebrew says “cut off your hair” with a feminine form (addressed to Jerusalem); NASB does not mark this.
